transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Naomi Ruiz (Redwood CSM); Lena Ortiz (Head of Security, Sierra), Tom Baker (SRE), Priya Desai (Legal), Diego Marquez (Platform), Aisha Khan (Compliance)

Summary:
Quick runthrough of SOC 2 evidence, KMS topology and HSM usage, on-call escalation paths (PagerDuty + Slack), and BCDR expectations (RTO/RPO targets). Walked through an RTO scenario and agreed next steps for a live drill.

Topics covered:
- SOC 2 scope and evidence locations
- KMS key management, HSM usage, BYOK options
- Audit logs, retention, and export for legal/forensics
- Data residency (EU vs US controls) and encryption-at-rest/in-transit
- BCDR: RTO/RPO examples, automated failover, runbooks, and post-incident reporting
- Escalation: PagerDuty, Slack channels, SLAs and on-call rotations

Action items (recap): see action_items metadata above.

Transcript body:
00:00:04 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick roll call?
00:00:12 Lena Ortiz: Lena here for Sierra, I'm head of security. Tom's on for SRE. Priya from legal, Diego platform, Aisha compliance.
00:00:20 Maya Chen: Great. Arjun and Naomi from Redwood with me. We're planning a focused hour on SOC2 & KMS plus an on-call runthrough. We want to make sure our escalation paths and runbooks match your expectations.
00:00:35 Tom Baker: Yeah, high level — our main questions: how keys are protected (HSM?), audit log fidelity, and what happens in a region outage. RTO/RPO stuff.
00:00:48 Arjun Patel: Cool. For KMS, Redwood uses a delegated KMS model for hosted, we can do customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private — and there are HSM-backed options. Sorry if I say K V cache earlier in other calls, ha, that's different.
00:01:10 Priya Desai: Quick legal note — we need key custody detail and whether Redwood can provide proof of key rotation for at least 12 months. Also exportable logs for a forensic review.
00:01:23 Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll attach the KMS architecture doc and key rotation audit.
00:01:30 Diego Marquez: On residency: some of our data must stay in the EU; we need confirmation of data-at-rest controls and where audit logs are stored.
00:01:40 Arjun Patel: For residency, we pin model serving to region — logs can be routed to your EU account or exported to your SIEM. There are a couple of minor limitations on cross-region cache warming, but that won't affect sovereignty of stored customer data.
00:01:56 Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. On the BCDR side: what's Redwood's RTO/RPO SLA for Dedicated vs Hosted?
00:02:06 Arjun Patel: We typically set RTO targets differently for hosted vs dedicated. Hosted falls back to multi-region routing with model variants — we target sub-90s cold-failover for small traffic classes but for large committed Dedicated tenants we work with specific RTOs in contract. I'll be honest, some of this is negotiable and depends on capacity reservations.
00:02:30 Tom Baker: Can we walk through a failure scenario? Like, EU region loss, primary cluster gone, we need to failover to US region without data loss. What's the sequence and who phones who?
00:02:41 Maya Chen: Yeah let's do a simple runthrough.
00:02:45 Arjun Patel: Step 1: detection via Prometheus/alerting — automatic PagerDuty trigger for our infra on-call. Step 2: automated routing policy tries a local fallback model variant — if that fails, orchestrator falls back to cross-region pool. Step 3: if orchestration triggers a capacity scar, there's an escalation to ops manager for burst capacity.
00:03:05 Tom Baker: Who's the contact at Redwood for an escalation? A phone tree?
00:03:10 Naomi Ruiz: We maintain a 24/7 on-call with escalation to senior on-call, then to a designated ops lead. We'll share the PagerDuty escalation policy and a phone roster.
00:03:20 Priya Desai: We need contact names and contractual SLA windows for when surge capacity is required.
00:03:26 Maya Chen: We'll put names and SLA windows in the follow-up pack, yes.
00:03:30 00:03:30 (crosstalk) Aisha Khan: Is there a signed runbook example we can see?
00:03:36 Arjun Patel: I'll pull a sanitized runbook snippet. Quick note — our runbook references internal tooling (we call it 'orch' sometimes), so we'll sanitize that language for you.
00:03:50 Lena Ortiz: On the audit logs — retention and tamper-proofing? We run internal audits quarterly; need to demonstrate immutability for at least 6 months and export options.
00:04:03 Arjun Patel: Logs are stored with append-only flags, we support export to S3 with write-once permissions or to your SIEM via secure syslog. Retention configurable, default 180 days for hosted, longer for enterprise packages.
00:04:18 Diego Marquez: Do you support CMEK / BYOK?
00:04:22 Arjun Patel: Yes, customer-managed encryption keys are supported for Dedicated and Private, and BYOK for specific regions once contract is in place. HSM-backed option via KMS provider; we can document the key lifecycle and KMS rotation policy.
00:04:36 Tom Baker: During an incident, can we get raw KV cache dumps for debugging?
00:04:41 Arjun Patel: We can provide sanitized traces and cache meta data; full token-level dumps are sensitive — we have a procedure to scrub PII and would coordinate with your team and legal.
00:04:55 Priya Desai: That scrub process needs to be in writing.
00:04:59 Maya Chen: We'll include that as a doc snippet.
00:05:05 00:05:05 Maya Chen: Okay let's simulate a failure now — RTO scenario: primary EU cluster loses network at 15:10 UTC. Walkthrough stepwise.
00:05:12 Tom Baker: Go.
00:05:14 Arjun Patel: Detection at 15:10, PD page at 15:10:12. On-call confirms. Router policy tries prefix routing to local cache for 30s, then kicks a cross-region request at 15:10:45. All of this appears in audit logs with correlation IDs.
00:05:38 Lena Ortiz: How quickly are customer audit logs available for a forensic pull?
00:05:43 Arjun Patel: They are streamed within minutes to our internal pipeline; export to your S3 or SIEM typically completes within the hour for a standard export, faster with priority support.
00:05:56 Tom Baker: And RPO? Are we losing events if the in-memory KV cache isn't replicated?
00:06:03 Arjun Patel: We don't rely on active-active KV replication for all workloads — RPO depends on workload config. For strict RPO you can enable synchronous write-through to object storage; that impacts latency. We discussed trade-offs earlier in the POC notes.
00:06:18 Diego Marquez: So for our low-latency endpoints we might accept 30s RPO but for compliance logs we need zero data loss.
00:06:25 Arjun Patel: Exactly — we can map endpoints to profiles.
00:06:29 Lena Ortiz: About SSO: does Redwood support SAML and SCIM provisioning? We need SSO into the console and audit of sign-ins.
00:06:36 Maya Chen: Yes, we support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM user provisioning. Login events show up in audit logs with IPs and device IDs.
00:06:45 Aisha Khan: Is there an RBAC matrix? We need admin, security-reader, billing roles, etc.
00:06:51 Naomi Ruiz: We have a role matrix; we'll attach it. There's also fine-grained route-level permissions for model access.
00:06:58 Priya Desai: On legal — retention and export clause language? Any standard addendums for e-discovery?
00:07:05 Maya Chen: We have an e-discovery addendum. We'll share the clause and sample request flow.
00:07:12 Tom Baker: Back to runbooks and the drill, who's running the firecall?
00:07:16 Maya Chen: Proposed run: Sierra leads the incident commander, Redwood provides ops liaison plus a communications lead. Naomi will coordinate the playbook and timeline.
00:07:26 Diego Marquez: We prefer Sierra IC for internal alignment, that works.
00:07:30 Arjun Patel: During the drill we will exercise the PagerDuty escalation: page infra-oncall, infra acknowledges, then ops lead, then exec on-call. We'll also simulate a KMS failover (read-only fallback) and document the impacts.
00:07:45 Lena Ortiz: Can Redwood demonstrate an HSM certificate or attestation for keys?
00:07:50 Arjun Patel: Yes, for HSM-backed keys we can provide attestation from the cloud KMS vendor; for Private on-prem we can provide HSM configs and evidence of FIPS compliance.
00:07:59 Priya Desai: For the contractual SLA—what uptime percentage and credits?
00:08:05 Maya Chen: For hosted we publish best-effort SLAs; Dedicated/Enterprise includes contractual uptime and credit terms. We'll share a sample SLA and the credit calculation.
00:08:15 Tom Baker: We need to check how long incident postmortems are retained and how quickly we get RCA.
00:08:21 Naomi Ruiz: Standard is a preliminary incident summary within 24 hours and a full RCA within 7-10 business days; we can adjust in contract.
00:08:30 Aisha Khan: On notification channels — email/Slack/PagerDuty — do you support cross-tenant webhooks to our internal Ops channel?
00:08:37 Arjun Patel: Yes, we support outbound webhooks configured per account; we can send structured incident payloads to your secured endpoint.
00:08:45 00:08:45 (background noise)
00:08:55 Tom Baker: One more: for forensics we may need packet captures or request IDs; can Redwood provide correlation IDs with each request?
00:09:02 Arjun Patel: Every request gets a correlation ID, request trace with timestamps, and we can surface that in logs and in trace exports.
00:09:12 Lena Ortiz: Good. Let's talk about the live drill scheduling and who needs to be present.
00:09:18 Maya Chen: We recommend the SRE on-call, platform lead, security incident lead, and legal observer. Naomi will send an invite that includes the scenario and expected outcomes.
00:09:28 Naomi Ruiz: I'll circulate a checklist and pre-read — runbook snippet, escalation policy, and sample audit exports.
00:09:34 Diego Marquez: For the scenario, please include KMS read-only failover and cross-region capacity shortages — those are our biggest concerns.
00:09:43 Arjun Patel: Noted. We'll prepare a script that hits both flows.
00:09:47 Priya Desai: Also include the data retention export flow for e-discovery, legal will want to see the timeline.
00:09:53 Maya Chen: We'll include that.
00:10:00 00:10:00 (meeting moves into deeper Q&A, timestamps abbreviated)
00:10:30 Tom Baker: During cross-region failover, are there any model fidelity differences? Will models be quantized differently?
00:10:38 Arjun Patel: There can be model variant differences, yes. We tend to have lighter quantized variants in some regions to save capacity; we document behavioral differences in the runbook and we recommend smoke tests post-failover.
00:10:55 Lena Ortiz: From compliance perspective, we need a changelog showing model variant used per request for auditability.
00:11:02 Arjun Patel: We can log model version and variant per request in audit logs.
00:11:10 Priya Desai: Any regulatory concerns for data crossing borders during cross-region failover?
00:11:15 Maya Chen: We highlight that cross-region failover moves transient in-flight requests; we provide contractual controls to restrict failover if you need strict residency — e.g., we can disable auto failover and require manual approval.
00:11:29 Tom Baker: Okay, last thing — if we see a sustained outage your mitigation steps include graceful degradation and fallback to cached responses?
00:11:37 Arjun Patel: Yes, prefix caching and KV cache serve as graceful degradation; we can also return structured degraded responses with a header that indicates partial content.
00:11:48 Lena Ortiz: That helps for user-facing features.
00:11:51 Maya Chen: We're almost at time. Quick recap of next steps: we'll send SOC2 evidence and KMS architecture, share PagerDuty escalation policy, propose a drill date, and attach runbook snippets.
00:12:04 Tom Baker: Sounds good.
00:12:07 Priya Desai: We'll review docs and circle back with any contract redlines.
00:12:11 Maya Chen: Thanks all — we'll get those to you by Thursday.
01:02:00 (meeting end)
